rationale: The Court is most likely to issue a narrow, institutionally cautious opinion dismissing for lack of Article III standing, emphasizing attenuation, third-party causation, and weak redressability under Clapper/Lyons/Summers. Separate concurrences are most likely from justices inclined to elaborate on originalist limits (Thomas), third-party causation (Gorsuch/Alito), or redressability/forward-looking relief (Barrett).
